ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Since December 2019, the COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the global economy. Frequent disinfection is a crucial preventive measure. As shown in the figure, a certain type of spray disinfection barrel and its schematic diagram are used for epidemic prevention and disinfection. The total volume of the disinfection barrel is 10L. After filling it with 7L of liquid medicine, the barrel is sealed with a lid. The piston-type air pump connected to the liquid storage cylinder can compress $250\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ of air at 1atm each time. Assume that the temperature remains constant throughout the entire process.

1. How many times should the pump be pressed to achieve an air pressure of 5atm in the sterilizing barrel?
2. When the air pressure in the gas cylinder reaches 5 atm, the nozzle is opened to spray until the internal and external gas pressures are equal, and the disinfectant no longer sprays outward. Is there any disinfectant left in the disinfection cylinder? If there is, what volume of disinfectant remains? If not, what fraction of the original gas mass in the disinfection cylinder before spraying is the mass of the gas that was sprayed out?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
48
The remaining gas cannot be retained, and the ejected gas accounts for \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the gas mass before ejection.

On the left is a sealed liquid storage bucket; in the lower part of the bucket a liquid region is drawn, and in the upper part a gas space is left; on the top of the bucket there is a sealing cover and connecting parts. On the left there is a pipe leading to the nozzle, and the pipe opening is used to spray out liquid. On the right is connected a piston-type air pump; the piston communicates with the liquid storage bucket through a pipe, used to press air into the bucket. Reasoning: The total volume of the disinfection bucket is 10 L. After 7 L of medicinal liquid is put in, the gas volume in the bucket is 10-7=3 L. The initial gas can be regarded as 1 atm, 3 L. The temperature is unchanged; according to the ideal gas relation, the amount of gas is proportional to PV. If it is necessary to reach 5 atm when the gas volume is still 3 L, then the amount of gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. Initially there is already PV=1×3=3 atm·L, so 12 atm·L of air needs to be added. Each pumping presses in 250 cm^3=0.25 L of air at 1 atm, namely 0.25 atm·L, so the required number of times is 12/0.25=48 times. Before spraying, the gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. If during the spraying process the gas does not leak outward and only relies on gas expansion to drop to 1 atm, then the required gas volume is 15 L, but the total volume of the disinfection bucket is only 10 L. Therefore when all 7 L of medicinal liquid is sprayed out and the gas fills 10 L, the air pressure in the bucket is still 15/10=1.5 atm, greater than the external 1 atm, so there will be no medicinal liquid remaining. After that the gas continues to leak outward, until the remaining gas in the bucket has a pressure of 1 atm in 10 L, corresponding to PV=10 atm·L. The amount of gas before spraying corresponds to 15 atm·L, and the final remaining amount of gas corresponds to 10 atm·L, so the proportion of the mass of the sprayed-out gas to the mass of the gas before spraying is (15-10)/15=1/3.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the diagram shows a sealed liquid barrel with a liquid region and a gas headspace above it, a hand piston pump connected to the barrel, and a spray tube/nozzle that draws liquid from near the bottom. Then reason by mole inventory using the ideal gas law. From the text, the barrel volume is 10 L and it contains 7 L liquid, so the gas volume before pumping is 3 L at 1 atm. To reach 5 atm at the same 3 L gas volume, the gas amount must increase from 1*3 to 5*3 = 15 atm·L, so the added amount is 12 atm·L. Each pump stroke adds 250 cm^3 = 0.25 L of air at 1 atm, i.e. 0.25 atm·L, so the required strokes are 12/0.25 = 48. For spraying, before opening the nozzle the gas has PV = 5*3 = 15 atm·L. If all gas stayed in the barrel while liquid was expelled, the gas volume needed to fall to 1 atm would be 15 L, but the whole barrel is only 10 L. Therefore the pressure is still above atmospheric when all liquid has been sprayed out, so no disinfectant remains. At that moment the gas volume is 10 L and its pressure would be 15/10 = 1.5 atm; gas then escapes until the remaining gas is 1 atm in 10 L. The gas mass decreases from proportional amount 15 to 10, so the ejected fraction is (15 - 10)/15 = 1/3.

推理：消毒桶总体积为10 L，装入7 L药液后，桶内气体体积为10-7=3 L。初始气体可看作1 atm、3 L。温度不变，按理想气体关系，气体量与PV成正比。若要在气体体积仍为3 L时达到5 atm，则桶内气体量对应PV=5×3=15 atm·L。初始已有PV=1×3=3 atm·L，因此需要增加12 atm·L的空气。每次打气压入250 cm^3=0.25 L、1 atm的空气，即0.25 atm·L，所以需要次数为12/0.25=48次。

喷雾前桶内气体对应PV=5×3=15 atm·L。若喷雾过程中气体不外泄，只靠气体膨胀降到1 atm，则所需气体体积为15 L，但消毒桶总容积只有10 L。因此当7 L药液全部喷出、气体占满10 L时，桶内气压仍为15/10=1.5 atm，大于外界1 atm，所以不会有药液剩余。之后气体继续外泄，直到桶内剩余气体在10 L中压强为1 atm，对应PV=10 atm·L。喷雾前气体量对应15 atm·L，最终剩余气体量对应10 atm·L，喷出的气体质量占喷雾前气体质量的比例为(15-10)/15=1/3。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the apparatus consists of a partly filled sealed sprayer barrel, a hand pump feeding air into the upper gas space, and a spray outlet connected by a tube into the liquid, so spraying reduces liquid volume and increases gas volume. Treat the gas state by an isothermal P-V path. Initially the air pocket is 10 - 7 = 3 L at 1 atm. The target state before spraying is 3 L at 5 atm, so the gas must contain the same amount as 15 L of air at 1 atm. Since it initially contains the same amount as 3 L of air at 1 atm, the pump must supply 12 L of equivalent atmospheric air. With 0.25 L per stroke, the stroke count is 48. For part 2, follow the isothermal curve from the state (V, P) = (3 L, 5 atm), so P = 15/V. The largest possible gas volume inside the barrel is 10 L, reached only after all 7 L of liquid has been expelled. At V = 10 L, the pressure on this curve is P = 15/10 = 1.5 atm, still greater than outside pressure. Thus the curve would not reach P = 1 atm until V = 15 L, which is impossible inside the barrel; hence all disinfectant has already left. After that, gas escapes at fixed barrel volume 10 L until P = 1 atm. Comparing gas amounts before and after gas escape gives initial proportional amount 5*3 = 15 and final proportional amount 1*10 = 10, so the escaped fraction is 5/15 = 1/3.

先描述图像：图中是一个喷雾消毒桶示意装置。桶内下部装有液体，液体用许多短横虚线表示；桶上部留有空气空间。左侧有喷嘴和导管，导管伸入桶内液体区域，用于把液体喷出。右侧有活塞式手压气泵，通过管道与桶相连，向密封桶内压入空气。因此喷液过程中，桶内液体体积减少，气体占据的体积增大。

再推理：消毒桶总体积为10 L，装入7 L药液后，初始空气体积为10 - 7 = 3 L。初始气压取1 atm，温度恒定，气体物质的量与PV成正比。

1. 要使桶内空气压强达到5 atm，而药液尚未喷出时气体体积仍为3 L，则桶内空气量相当于1 atm下的体积：5 × 3 = 15 L。初始桶内空气量相当于1 atm下的3 L，所以还需压入相当于15 - 3 = 12 L的1 atm空气。每次气泵压入250 cm^3 = 0.25 L的1 atm空气，所以按压次数为12 ÷ 0.25 = 48次。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the figure shows a closed sprayer reservoir, a pump connected to it, a liquid-filled lower portion, an air space at the top, and a nozzle tube capable of discharging the contents. Use an equivalent-atmospheric-volume bookkeeping method. The initial gas space is 3 L, so initially the barrel contains 3 'liters at 1 atm' of air. The desired pressure 5 atm in the same 3 L space corresponds to 15 equivalent liters at 1 atm. The required added equivalent air is therefore 15 - 3 = 12 L. Because one pump stroke supplies 0.25 equivalent liters, the number of strokes is 12/0.25 = 48. For spraying, before the nozzle opens the barrel contains 15 equivalent liters of air. If liquid were left at the end, the remaining gas would occupy less than 10 L and be at 1 atm, so it could contain less than 10 equivalent liters; but the gas would have to have expanded without leaving while the tube was still submerged in liquid. Since the 15 equivalent liters of gas cannot be accommodated at 1 atm within the maximum 10 L barrel volume, the gas remains overpressure until all liquid has been expelled. Therefore no disinfectant remains. Once the barrel contains only gas, at final equilibrium it can hold only 10 equivalent liters at 1 atm, so 15 - 10 = 5 equivalent liters of the original pre-spray gas leaves. The fraction ejected is 5/15 = 1/3.

This matches a closed sprayer in which compressed air above the liquid pushes disinfectant out through the nozzle.

Reasoning: The barrel volume is 10 L and it is filled with 7 L of liquid, so the initial air volume is 3 L. At constant temperature, use equivalent volume of air at 1 atm to track gas amount. Initially, the air in the barrel is 3 L at 1 atm, i.e. 3 equivalent liters. To reach 5 atm while the gas volume remains 3 L, the barrel must contain 5 × 3 = 15 equivalent liters of air. Thus the added air needed is 15 - 3 = 12 L at 1 atm. Each pump stroke supplies 250 cm^3 = 0.25 L of air at 1 atm, so the required number of strokes is 12 / 0.25 = 48.

Before spraying, the barrel contains 15 equivalent liters of air. While liquid remains, the gas has not escaped through the liquid outlet; it expands as liquid is expelled. If spraying stopped with liquid still left and internal pressure equal to the outside pressure of 1 atm, the gas would have to occupy 15 L, but the entire barrel capacity is only 10 L. This is impossible. Therefore the liquid must be completely expelled first. When the barrel just becomes all gas, the gas occupies 10 L, so its pressure is 15 / 10 = 1.5 atm, still above atmospheric pressure. Then gas continues to escape until the pressure becomes 1 atm. At the end, the 10 L barrel contains 10 equivalent liters of air, so the amount of gas expelled is 15 - 10 = 5 equivalent liters. The fraction of the original pre-spray gas mass that is expelled is 5 / 15 = 1/3.

raw_record.original_question:
Since December 2019, the COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the global economy. Frequent disinfection is a crucial preventive measure. As shown in the figure, a certain type of spray disinfection barrel and its schematic diagram are used for epidemic prevention and disinfection. The total volume of the disinfection barrel is 10L. After filling it with 7L of liquid medicine, the barrel is sealed with a lid. The piston-type air pump connected to the liquid storage cylinder can compress $250\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ of air at 1atm each time. Assume that the temperature remains constant throughout the entire process.

1. How many times should the pump be pressed to achieve an air pressure of 5atm in the sterilizing barrel?
2. When the air pressure in the gas cylinder reaches 5 atm, the nozzle is opened to spray until the internal and external gas pressures are equal, and the disinfectant no longer sprays outward. Is there any disinfectant left in the disinfection cylinder? If there is, what volume of disinfectant remains? If not, what fraction of the original gas mass in the disinfection cylinder before spraying is the mass of the gas that was sprayed out?
raw_record.answer:
48
The remaining gas cannot be retained, and the ejected gas accounts for \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the gas mass before ejection

Image description: The figure is a structural schematic diagram of a spray disinfection bucket. On the left is a sealed liquid storage bucket; in the lower part of the bucket a liquid region is drawn, and in the upper part a gas space is left; on the top of the bucket there is a sealing cover and connecting parts. On the left there is a pipe leading to the nozzle, and the pipe opening is used to spray out liquid. On the right is connected a piston-type air pump; the piston communicates with the liquid storage bucket through a pipe, used to press air into the bucket.

Reasoning: The total volume of the disinfection bucket is 10 L. After 7 L of medicinal liquid is put in, the gas volume in the bucket is 10-7=3 L. The initial gas can be regarded as 1 atm, 3 L. The temperature is unchanged; according to the ideal gas relation, the amount of gas is proportional to PV. If it is necessary to reach 5 atm when the gas volume is still 3 L, then the amount of gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. Initially there is already PV=1×3=3 atm·L, so 12 atm·L of air needs to be added. Each pumping presses in 250 cm^3=0.25 L of air at 1 atm, namely 0.25 atm·L, so the required number of times is 12/0.25=48 times.

Before spraying, the gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. If during the spraying process the gas does not leak outward and only relies on gas expansion to drop to 1 atm, then the required gas volume is 15 L, but the total volume of the disinfection bucket is only 10 L. Therefore when all 7 L of medicinal liquid is sprayed out and the gas fills 10 L, the air pressure in the bucket is still 15/10=1.5 atm, greater than the external 1 atm, so there will be no medicinal liquid remaining. After that the gas continues to leak outward, until the remaining gas in the bucket has a pressure of 1 atm in 10 L, corresponding to PV=10 atm·L. The amount of gas before spraying corresponds to 15 atm·L, and the final remaining amount of gas corresponds to 10 atm·L, so the proportion of the mass of the sprayed-out gas to the mass of the gas before spraying is (15-10)/15=1/3.

Image description: The figure is a structural schematic diagram of a spray disinfection bucket. On the left is a sealed liquid storage bucket; in the lower part of the bucket a liquid region is drawn, and in the upper part a gas space is left; on the top of the bucket there is a sealing cover and connecting parts. On the left there is a pipe leading to the nozzle, and the pipe opening is used to spray out liquid. On the right is connected a piston-type air pump; the piston communicates with the liquid storage bucket through a pipe, used to press air into the bucket.

Reasoning: The total volume of the disinfection bucket is 10 L. After 7 L of medicinal liquid is put in, the gas volume in the bucket is 10-7=3 L. The initial gas can be regarded as 1 atm, 3 L. The temperature is unchanged; according to the ideal gas relation, the amount of gas is proportional to PV. If it is necessary to reach 5 atm when the gas volume is still 3 L, then the amount of gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. Initially there is already PV=1×3=3 atm·L, so 12 atm·L of air needs to be added. Each pumping presses in 250 cm^3=0.25 L of air at 1 atm, namely 0.25 atm·L, so the required number of times is 12/0.25=48 times.

Before spraying, the gas in the bucket corresponds to PV=5×3=15 atm·L. If during the spraying process the gas does not leak outward and only relies on gas expansion to drop to 1 atm, then the required gas volume is 15 L, but the total volume of the disinfection bucket is only 10 L. Therefore when all 7 L of medicinal liquid is sprayed out and the gas fills 10 L, the air pressure in the bucket is still 15/10=1.5 atm, greater than the external 1 atm, so there will be no medicinal liquid remaining. After that the gas continues to leak outward, until the remaining gas in the bucket has a pressure of 1 atm in 10 L, corresponding to PV=10 atm·L. The amount of gas before spraying corresponds to 15 atm·L, and the final remaining amount of gas corresponds to 10 atm·L, so the proportion of the mass of the sprayed-out gas to the mass of the gas before spraying is (15-10)/15=1/3.
